Title: Birol et al. (2002) Penicillin production in a fed-batch fermentor (extended Bajpai and Reuss model)

Abstract: Simulation software based on a detailed unstructured model for penicillin production in a fed-batch fermentor has been developed. The model extends the mechanistic model of Bajpai and Reuss by adding input variables such as pH, temperature, aeration rate, agitation power, and feed flow rate of substrate and introducing the CO₂ evolution term. The simulation package was then used for monitoring and fault diagnosis of a typical penicillin fermentation process. The simulator developed may be used for both research and educational purposes and is available at the web site: http://www.chee.iit.edu/~control/software.html.

Laws:
(1) [balance] The law balances biomass concentration through growth and the effect of changing culture volume.
(3) [constitutive] The law computes specific growth rate from glucose and oxygen availability, pH inhibition, and Arrhenius growth and death effects.
(9) [balance] The law balances penicillin concentration through non-growth-associated production, hydrolysis, and dilution.
(10) [constitutive] The law computes the specific penicillin production rate with substrate inhibition and oxygen dependence.
(11) [balance] The law balances glucose concentration through consumption for growth, penicillin production and maintenance, plus feed and dilution.
(12) [balance] The law balances dissolved oxygen concentration through cellular consumption, gas-liquid transfer, and dilution.
(13) [constitutive] The law computes the overall mass-transfer coefficient from oxygen flow rate and agitation power per culture volume.
(14) [balance] The law balances fermentor culture volume by adding substrate feed and acid/base addition and subtracting evaporative loss.
(15) [constitutive] The law computes evaporative volume loss as a temperature- and volume-dependent rate.
(16) [constitutive] The law computes microbial heat-generation rate from biomass growth and a biomass-proportional maintenance contribution.
(17) [balance] The law balances fermentor temperature using feed-temperature effects, reaction heat, and cooling-coil heat removal.
(18) [constitutive] The law computes CO2 evolution from growth, biomass-associated maintenance, and a constant production-associated contribution.

- X: Biomass concentration.

- S: Substrate concentration.
- C_{L}: Dissolved oxygen concentration.
- V: Culture volume.

- P_{w}: Agitation power input
- F_{a/b}: Acid/base addition term contributing to broth volume change

answer.description: This is a dynamic fed-batch fermentation model for penicillin production, with Penicillium chrysogenum inferred from the cited Bajpai–Reuss model. It predicts biomass, penicillin, substrate, dissolved oxygen, culture volume, temperature, heat generation, and CO₂. Growth depends on glucose and oxygen and includes pH and temperature effects; penicillin production is non-growth-associated, substrate-inhibited, and oxygen-dependent, with additional balances for oxygen transfer, heat, evaporation, and CO₂.
